MTA Copy Master Series
Riddled with Language
Practical Exercises in Language Skills
A.R. Gillon
Modern Teaching Aids Pty Ltd (Incorporated in NSW), 26-28 Chard Road, Brookvale, N.S.W. 2100. (02) 939 2355

Children love RIDDLES. Riddles are complete Comprehension exercises in themselves. With this in mind, I have compiled these practical exercises in LANGUAGE skills.
The “RIDDLER’S STORIES” in this book contain answers to three or more riddles, interwoven through the story, motivating the pupil to read each passage carefully.
The Language exercises that follow provide the pupil with a comprehensive coverage of SPEAKING, WRITING and READING skills.
In each UNIT there are exercises in:
1. PRONUNCIATION 2. SOUNDS (and PHONIC SKILLS) 3. WORD ANALYSIS and ATTACK 4, SENTENCE STRUCTURE 5. GRAMMAR 6. PUNCTUATION (USAGE) 7. VOCABULARY 8. HANDWRITING 9. WRITTEN EXPRESSION
Also included for the child’s enjoyment are:
1. JOKETIME CORNERS 2. FIND-A-WORD PUZZLES 3. WHO AM I? QUESTIONS
This book enables the pupil to learn language skills through brief enjoyable exercises, without the barrier of formal, indigestible English lessons.
A.R. GILLON

The Riddler’s Story THE FLEXIBLE COBBLER
Nowadays, cobblers use a variety of materials when making shoes. Canvas, nylon, rubber and pig skins are very useful and efficient. A clever cobbler down Sole Street tried using banana peel too. It was not very good for school shoes but it made handy slippers.
This shoemaker experiments a lot with left shoes, but never gets them quite right. With his head down, the shoemaker hammers and stitches right through the day. To help school shoes wear longer, he leaves the nail head exposed in the sole of the shoe, The little nails must get a headache walking around upside down all day.
Who knows what this eccentric cobbler will do next? Perhaps he will call in the elves and leprechauns.

The Riddler’s Story
DOWN ON THE FARM
Being a farmer sure has its headaches. One day it’s flooding and your crops are ruined, the next day begins a long, grim drought. Perhaps that explains the actions of
Bill Freeman with his “get-rich-quick” schemes. Bill lives on Bald Hill, high above his dairy down below, overlooking his vast potato crops in the valley. His dairy cows were not producing good-quality, rich milk though. Each day he fed them bales of hay to improve the quality of the milk. It wasn’t until he added a quantity of crisp, five dollar notes to the feed that things improved. The cows produced just what he wanted - rich milk.
Another scheme started when his potato crop was ruined. Bill ploughed the plants in with a steam roller. That really smashed the potato crop. He said, ‘Now I’m the only one growing mashed potatoes, I’ll make millions.”
Bill now takes pills for his headaches. You know how hard pills are to get down; and you know how hard hills are to get up; well Bill faces both of these problems each day as he walks on Bald Hill.

Have you ever seen the ONE-DAY CRICKET matches on TV? It is really exciting to watch the spectators in the stands. What a bunch. Between bowls and shouts, you can some busily making sunshades and fans out of newspaper.
One spectator, who was extra hot, quickly moved out of the sun to sit near his mate, a real cricket fan. “Sitting near you should keep me cool,” he said. Some of the revellers were wearing “wash and wear” jeans, soaking wet. One boy had washed them and worn them straight to the match, wet, obeying the instructions on the label.
One of the batsmen completely missed the ball. It skimmed right through to the wicket keeper. ‘’Howzat?”’ they screamed. ‘He didn’t meet Cinderella that time,”

The Riddler’s Story
DOWN IN THE DUNGEON
Below the castle on Ifnii Island, there is a maze of dark dungeons. Although tne castle is uninhabited, we can’t say the same for the dungeons. Witches busily vacuum around their cauldrons each day, clearing away excess herbs and lizards’ tails.
A number of ghosts move from room to room sweeping and making the beds. They need only one key, a skeleton key, to pass through the firmly fastened doors. Speaking of skeletons, they pull their weight too, working their fingers to the bones. There’s one tired skeleton though. His name is Aaron. They sing the song
“Lazybones” about him.
Really, that is what they should CALL him. He’s always too tired to work.
When the work is done, the witches put away their heavy vacuum cleaners, Although we live in an electrical age, they choose to fly about on lighter, smaller broomsticks.
(Vacuum cleaners are much too heavy!) It sure is a hive of activity down in the dungeons.
